questionText: How do you map HTTP methods to Spring Boot controller annotations?

target.learningOutcome: The learner can map common HTTP methods and paths to Spring MVC controller methods, bind request input, validate a DTO, and return the intended HTTP status, headers, and body.
inScope: Path, query, and body argument binding
One controller excerpt and request-flow diagram
prerequisites: Basic HTTP method and status semantics

claims.statement: Spring MVC provides GetMapping, PostMapping, PutMapping, PatchMapping, and DeleteMapping as HTTP-method-specific composed variants of RequestMapping.
RequestMapping can declare a shared class-level mapping and a method-level mapping can narrow it to one path, HTTP method, media type, parameter, or header condition.
PathVariable reads URI-template values, RequestParam reads request parameters, and RequestBody delegates request-content conversion to an HttpMessageConverter.
A request-body command object annotated with Valid is eligible for Bean Validation before normal controller processing when a Bean Validation implementation is configured.
RestController combines Controller and ResponseBody semantics, so supported return values are written through response handling rather than being treated as view names.
ResponseEntity represents a complete HTTP response value whose body is converted through message converters and whose status and headers are supplied explicitly.
Selecting a Spring handler does not itself enforce HTTP method semantics; the endpoint implementation must still preserve properties such as GET safety and PUT idempotency.

notes: The code is intentionally a focused controller excerpt; it uses an explicit path-variable name and does not pretend to be a runnable application with service and persistence implementations.
Spring MVC is the mapping implementation; Spring Boot supplies the managed baseline and typical web auto-configuration.
